headline: Proposed rollback of Mass. health aide program previews the coming pain from Medicaid cuts
summary: Massachusetts faces a projected $3.5 billion annual loss in federal Medicaid aid beginning next year, creating severe pressure on the FY 2027 state budget which already proposes $100 million in cuts to the Personal Care Attendant program and level-funding for health care providers. Governor Healey’s administration is considering tapping 15 percent ($1.2 billion) of the state’s $8 billion “rainy day” fund, rejecting Trump-era corporate tax cuts to preserve $463 million in state revenue, and pursuing corporate fair share legislation to generate $400 million annually to offset the deficit. These budget decisions reflect a shift toward austerity measures that may increase long-term costs by forcing vulnerable residents into higher-cost care settings while lawmakers weigh revenue generation against service cuts.

headline: US Senate tees up final vote on Mullin confirmation to lead Homeland Security
summary: The U.S. Senate voted to advance Markwayne Mullin’s nomination to lead the Department of Homeland Security, which has been shut down since February 14 amid a stalemate over changes to immigration enforcement policy. Senate Democrats have blocked funding for the department following the deaths of two U.S. citizens during a months-long immigrant enforcement operation in Minneapolis. If confirmed, Mullin will oversee the agency responsible for enforcing President Trump’s aggressive immigration policy, succeeding outgoing Secretary Kristi Noem, who faced bipartisan criticism for describing victims of the Minneapolis shootings as domestic terrorists without evidence.

headline: How RFK Jr.’s vaccine agenda risks resurgence of deadly childhood plagues
summary: The article warns that federal vaccine policy changes under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.—including removing vaccines from the CDC’s recommended schedule, cutting $1.6 billion in global immunization aid, and appointing vaccine skeptics to advisory panels—threaten to trigger outbreaks of preventable diseases like measles and Hib in Louisiana and nationwide. Dr. Evelyn Griffin, a Baton Rouge physician appointed by Gov. Jeff Landry as Louisiana’s Surgeon General, serves on the reconstituted CDC vaccine advisory panel that has reduced routine childhood immunization recommendations. These governmental shifts risk dismantling manufacturer liability protections and reducing access to shots, potentially reviving diseases previously eliminated in the U.S. and endangering public health infrastructure.
